# linux_cron_job (Resource)

Manages a job in the crontab of a user, like Ansible's `cron`. The job is tagged with a `# Terraform: <name>` comment, and the other entries of the crontab are left untouched. Requires `crontab` on the host.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "linux_cron_job" "backup" {
  name     = "nightly backup"
  user     = "root"
  schedule = "30 2 * * *"
  command  = "/usr/local/bin/backup > /var/log/backup.log 2>&1"
}

resource "linux_cron_job" "cleanup" {
  name     = "tmp cleanup"
  schedule = "@daily"
  command  = "find /tmp -type f -mtime +7 -delete"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `command` (String) Command to run. In a crontab, `%` means a new line unless escaped as `\%`.
- `name` (String) Name identifying the job in the crontab.
- `schedule` (String) When the job runs: five fields, such as `*/15 * * * *`, or a nickname such as `@daily` or `@reboot`.

### Optional

- `disabled` (Boolean) Keep the job commented out. Defaults to `false`.
- `user` (String) User whose crontab holds the job. Defaults to the user running the commands.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) User and name of the job.
